message.content: Trade increased the pharaoh’s power. He controlled the routes, goods, and customs, so their profits became his taxes. It gave him resources for armies, temples, and monuments. The people felt that he fed them, protected them, and rewarded their loyal workers. Those goods also made his court look rich to visitors, who then respected his authority. If trade failed, they blamed him, and their complaints could weaken his throne. We can see that he used those networks to make his rule seem wider, stronger, and more connected than it was to them.
